학생.e: Literally 'learning life' — someone whose life is learning.
학생.t: Pronounced [학쌩]: ㅅ after a ㄱ batchim becomes tense ㅆ.

권.forms: native number + 권: 책 세 권
권.x: I borrowed two books from the library.
권.e: Originally 'scroll'; 책 두 권 = two books.

벌.forms: native number + 벌: 옷 한 벌 · 바지 두 벌
벌.m: counter for clothes (an outfit, a garment, a suit)
벌.x: I bought two outfits at the department store.
벌.e: 옷 한 벌 = one outfit or garment. Homonym: 벌 also means bee.

걱정.ex: 시험 걱정 때문에 어젯밤에 잠을 못 잤어요.
걱정.x: I couldn't sleep last night because I was worried about the exam.
걱정.e: Becomes verbs easily: 걱정하다 (to worry), 걱정되다 (to feel worried).
걱정.t: Pronounced [걱쩡]; 걱정 마세요 is the everyday way to say 'Don't worry.'

눈이 오다.forms: 눈이 와요 · 눈이 왔어요 · 눈이 올 거예요
눈이 오다.ex: 어젯밤에 눈이 많이 와서 길이 미끄러워요.
눈이 오다.x: It snowed a lot last night, so the roads are slippery.
눈이 오다.e: Literally 'snow comes'; 눈 also means 'eye', but context makes it clear.

반바지.ex: 저는 여름에 더워서 반바지를 자주 입어요.
반바지.x: I often wear shorts in the summer because it's hot.

절대로.ex: 이 비밀은 절대로 다른 사람에게 말하지 마세요.
절대로.x: Never tell this secret to anyone else.
절대로.e: Literally 'cut off from any opposite' — absolute, beyond comparison.
절대로.t: Pronounced [절때로]; mostly used with negatives like 안, 못 or -지 마세요.

회.forms: Use with Sino numbers: 1회, 2회, 3회 (일 회, 이 회, 삼 회)
회.x: This class meets twice a week.
회.e: The formal, written counterpart of 번; seen on schedules, labels and TV episodes.
회.t: In everyday speech say 두 번 'twice'; 2회 sounds formal and appears mostly in writing.

영업.x: I'm in charge of sales at my company.
영업.t: On shop signs, 영업 중 means 'Open'; 영업 시간 means business hours.

증상.ex: 감기 증상이 있으면 집에서 푹 쉬세요.
증상.x: If you have cold symptoms, get plenty of rest at home.
증상.t: Doctors often ask 어떤 증상이 있으세요? — 'What symptoms do you have?'

주민 센터.m: community service center, local neighborhood office
주민 센터.ex: 주민 센터에서 무료 한국어 수업을 들어요.
주민 센터.x: I take a free Korean class at the community service center.
주민 센터.t: It used to be called 동사무소, and older people may still use that name.

적응하다.ex: 새 학교에 적응하는 데 한 달쯤 걸렸어요.
적응하다.x: It took me about a month to adjust to my new school.
적응하다.t: Mark what you adapt to with 에: 새 환경에 적응하다 (adapt to a new environment).

언론사.x: Several news outlets reported on the incident.
언론사.e: 언론 'the press' + -사 'company'; -사 = company: 방송사, 신문사, 여행사.
언론사.t: Pronounced [얼론사]: ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

무심코.ex: 무심코 한 말이 친구에게 상처를 줬어요.
무심코.x: Something I said without thinking hurt my friend.

반하다.forms: Mostly as connectors: N에 반해 · N에 반하여 · N에 반하는 (+noun)
반하다.m: to be contrary to, to go against; to contrast with
반하다.x: Contrary to expectations, the result wasn't good.
반하다.e: Literally 'to be opposite'; homonym warning: native 반하다 means 'to fall for someone'.
반하다.t: Don't confuse 기대에 반해 'contrary to expectations' with 그녀에게 반했어요 'I fell for her'.

육성하다.m: to foster, to nurture, to develop (talent, industry)
육성하다.x: The government announced a policy to foster small businesses.

거두다.m: to harvest, to gather; to achieve (results); to take back
거두다.ex: 우리 팀이 이번 경기에서 큰 승리를 거두었어요.
거두다.x: Our team won a big victory in this game.
거두다.e: Its short form 걷다 means 'to collect', as in 회비를 걷다.

꼬이다.m: to get twisted, to get tangled; to go wrong
꼬이다.x: Things went wrong from the start, so the plan got delayed.
꼬이다.e: Passive of 꼬다 'to twist', as in 다리를 꼬다 'to cross your legs'.
꼬이다.t: Homonym: 꼬이다 also means bugs swarming, as in 파리가 꼬이다.

넘치다.m: to overflow, to brim over; to be full of
넘치다.ex: 그 가수의 무대는 언제나 에너지가 넘쳐요.
넘치다.x: That singer's performances are always full of energy.
넘치다.e: Related to 넘다 'to go over': liquid going over the edge.

귀를 기울이다.forms: 귀를 기울여요 · 귀를 기울였어요 · N에 귀를 기울이다
귀를 기울이다.m: to listen carefully, to lend an ear, to pay attention to
귀를 기울이다.ex: 정부는 시민들의 목소리에 귀를 기울여야 합니다.
귀를 기울이다.x: The government must listen to the voices of its citizens.
귀를 기울이다.e: Literally 'to tilt one's ear' toward a sound.

좌절감.ex: 여러 번 실패하면서 큰 좌절감을 느꼈어요.
좌절감.x: After failing several times, I felt deeply frustrated.
rel: to be frustrated, to give up

광복.m: liberation (of Korea in 1945), restoration of independence

학식.x: He is very learned and has a fine character.
학식.t: Homonym: students also say 학식 for a school cafeteria meal (from 학생 식당).

역력하다.x: Fatigue was plainly visible on his face.
역력하다.e: The same syllable doubled for emphasis: 'clear, clear'.
역력하다.t: Pronounced [영녀카다]; usually with 기색, 표정, 흔적.

권선징악.m: rewarding good and punishing evil; poetic justice
권선징악.x: Most old folktales are about good being rewarded and evil punished.

손사래를 치다.forms: 손사래를 쳐요 · 손사래를 쳤어요 · 손사래를 치며
손사래를 치다.m: to wave one's hand in refusal; to wave something off
손사래를 치다.ex: 칭찬을 하자 그는 손사래를 치며 웃었어요.
손사래를 치다.x: When I praised him, he waved it off and laughed.
손사래를 치다.e: 손사래 = waving your hand side to side; built on 손 'hand.'

위기감.m: sense of crisis, feeling of urgency
위기감.ex: 매출이 계속 줄어들자 직원들 사이에 위기감이 커졌어요.
위기감.x: As sales kept falling, a sense of crisis grew among the employees.
위기감.e: -감 = 'feeling, sense of': 위기감, 책임감, 자신감, 불안감.

고소득층.x: The government decided to raise taxes on high-income earners.
고소득층.e: Literally 'high income layer'. -층 = social group: 저소득층, 중산층.

악평.ex: 그 영화는 개봉 후에 악평을 많이 받았어요.
악평.x: That movie got a lot of bad reviews after it was released.
악평.t: Common patterns: 악평을 받다 'to get bad reviews' and 악평이 쏟아지다 'bad reviews pour in'; the opposite is 호평.

출사표.m: declaration of entry (into a race or competition)
출사표.ex: 그는 다음 시장 선거에 출사표를 던졌습니다.
출사표.x: He declared his candidacy for the next mayoral election.
출사표.e: From a famous memorial by the strategist Zhuge Liang before leading troops into battle.
출사표.t: Almost always used as 출사표를 던지다 (to throw one's hat in the ring).

떡밥.m: hint, foreshadowing, clue (for fans to speculate on)
떡밥.ex: 이번 화에 떡밥이 많아서 다음 화가 너무 궁금해요.
떡밥.x: This episode dropped so many hints that I'm dying to see the next one.
떡밥.e: Originally fishing bait made from grain paste (떡 'rice cake' + 밥 'rice'); slang for anything thrown out to hook fans.
떡밥.t: Pronounced [떡빱]. Casual/online. 떡밥을 던지다 = to drop a hint; 떡밥을 회수하다 = to pay it off later.

죽도 밥도 안 되다.forms: 죽도 밥도 안 됐어요 · 이러다 죽도 밥도 안 되겠어요
죽도 밥도 안 되다.m: to come to nothing, to end up a total mess (by doing things halfway) (lit. to become neither porridge nor rice)
죽도 밥도 안 되다.ex: 이것저것 다 하려다가 죽도 밥도 안 됐어요.
죽도 밥도 안 되다.x: I tried to do everything at once, and it all came to nothing.
죽도 밥도 안 되다.e: Botched cooking: with the wrong amount of water, the rice turns out neither proper porridge nor proper rice.
죽도 밥도 안 되다.t: Often a warning against doing things halfway or chasing two goals at once: 이러다 죽도 밥도 안 되겠어요.

허가제.ex: 이 지역에서는 노점 영업이 허가제로 운영돼요.
허가제.x: In this area, street vending is run on a permit system.
허가제.e: Literally 'permission system' — you must get approval before acting.
허가제.t: 허가제 needs approval first; 신고제 only needs you to notify the authorities.

기도문.ex: 아이들은 식사 전에 짧은 기도문을 외웠어요.
기도문.x: The children recited a short prayer before the meal.

성리학.x: Toegye Yi Hwang is a representative Neo-Confucian scholar of Joseon.
성리학.e: Literally 'study of human nature and principle'.
성리학.t: Pronounced [성니학] — ㄹ after ㅇ becomes ㄴ.

항성.m: star (that shines by itself), fixed star
항성.x: The sun is a star that produces its own light.
항성.e: Literally 'constant star' — it seems to stay in place, unlike planets.
항성.t: Easy to confuse: 항성 shines by itself, 행성 (planet) orbits it, and 위성 (moon) orbits a planet.

서사시.ex: 호메로스의 일리아스는 서양 문학의 대표적인 서사시입니다.
서사시.x: Homer's Iliad is a representative epic of Western literature.
서사시.e: Literally 'narrating-events poem' — a long poem that tells a story.

상류층.x: Mostly upper-class people live in that neighborhood.
상류층.t: Pronounced [상뉴층]: ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

아로새기다.m: to engrave intricately; to engrave in one's memory
아로새기다.x: I engraved my teacher's words deep in my heart.
아로새기다.e: 새기다 (to carve) + 아로-, suggesting fine, intricate detail (compare 아롱아롱).

에우다.x: The enemy surrounded the fortress layer upon layer and attacked.
에우다.e: The root of 에워싸다 'to surround'; probably related to 에두르다.
